# EvAspectRatio

> A box that holds one media element at a fixed width-to-height ratio, filling it with the media and clipping the overflow.

| --- | --- |
| ID | `evoq-ui:aspect-ratio` |
| Layer | Atom (`src/atoms`) |
| Import | `import { EvAspectRatio } from 'evoq-ui'` |

| Source | `src/atoms/aspect-ratio/EvAspectRatio.vue` |
| Extra attributes go to | the root `<div class="ev-aspect-ratio">` |

```vue

</EvAspectRatio>
```

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Aspect Ratio**, frame `4156:64491` (Aspect Ratio). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Wrap an image, video, map, or embed that must keep a consistent proportion as the layout resizes — preventing distortion and reflow.

### When not to use

- Content with intrinsic, variable height (text blocks, lists). Cases where the exact pixel size is fixed and known — size it directly instead.

### Do

- Place a single media element in the slot and let it fill. Pick the ratio that matches the source media. Use inside responsive grids and cards.

### Don't

- Don't put multiple unrelated elements in one Aspect Ratio. Don't override the height manually — let the ratio drive it.

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvAspectRatio`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<div class="ev-aspect-ratio">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:aspect-ratio` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
